findings.title: Harvest count and total weight are multiplied by the number of journal entries
findings.where: GET /api/plants, GET /api/plants/{id}; plants list and plant detail pages
findings.steps: Add 2 journal entries to Tomato (3 harvests, 1350 g). Open /plants or /plants/1, or call GET /api/plants/1.
findings.actual: harvest_count 6, harvest_grams 2700. PLANT_SELECT LEFT JOINs both harvests and journal_entries, which makes a cross product; COUNT(h.id) and SUM(h.weight_grams) are not de-duplicated.
findings.evidence: GET /api/plants/1 returned harvest_count=6, harvest_grams=2700, but its harvests array has 3 items summing to 1350 g. The delete-plant confirmation and the average-harvest figure use the same wrong numbers.

findings.title: Journal entry body containing a NUL character causes 500
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error. SQLite length() stops at the NUL, so the CHECK constraint fails with an IntegrityError that nothing catches.

findings.title: Out-of-range ids cause 500 on journal endpoints
Journal load errors have no retry, on both the Journal page and the plant journal section
findings.steps: Open /journal or a plant while the API is down or the journal request fails. Bring the API back.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that refetches without a reload
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown, with no retry control. On the plant page, the journal list and the empty state both disappear. The user has to reload, or on /journal change the search text.
findings.evidence: pages/journal.vue and pages/plants/[id].vue render AlertMessage for loadError/journalLoadError and nothing calls refresh

findings.title: Journal requests have no 10-second timeout
findings.where: useApiClient / useApiFetch used by the journal list, add, edit and delete
findings.steps: Make the API hang (stalled response) and add, save or delete an entry
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 s with a visible error and the button comes back
findings.actual: $fetch.create has no timeout, so 'Saving…' and disabled buttons stay that way for as long as the connection hangs
findings.evidence: composables/useApi.ts: no timeout option. JournalEntryForm/Item rely on the promise settling.

findings.title: Retrying an add after a timeout or network error creates duplicate entries
findings.where: POST /api/journal from the plant detail 'Add entry' form
findings.steps: Submit an entry; the response is lost or slow (server committed). The error shows and the text is kept; click Add entry again.
findings.actual: Two identical entries. The POST has no idempotency key and the server has no de-duplication.
findings.evidence: routers/journal.py create_entry inserts on every call. The client sends no request id.

findings.title: Search over 80 characters shows a raw validation error instead of results
findings.steps: Type or paste 81+ characters into Search
findings.expected: The input limits length or shows a friendly reason
findings.actual: The API returns 422 and the page replaces the list with 'Q: String should have at most 80 characters'. The input has no maxlength.
findings.evidence: GET /api/journal?q=<81 chars> -> 422 string_too_long; journal.vue input has no maxlength and shows the loadError

findings.title: Character limit counts UTF-16 units, so emoji entries are capped at 250 and server-valid entries can't be edited
findings.steps: Through the API, create an entry with 500 emoji (accepted, 201; entry id 4 on Tomato). Open Tomato and click Edit, then Save.
findings.expected: The 500-character limit is the same on client and server; an existing entry can be saved
findings.actual: The client uses String.length and textarea maxlength (UTF-16), so an emoji counts as 2. The edit form shows a negative 'characters left' count and validate() refuses with 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.' New entries hit the cap at 250 emoji.
findings.evidence: The API accepted 500 emoji (201). The form uses form.body.length and :maxlength=500.

findings.title: 'Today' differs between client and server, so valid dates can be refused or future dates allowed
findings.steps: Use a browser in a time zone ahead of the server (e.g. UTC+13) in the server's evening and pick today's local date
findings.actual: The server's date.today() (server local time) says it is in the future and returns 422 'Journal date cannot be in the future.', though the date picker allowed it
findings.evidence: Client uses the browser's local todayIso(); server uses date.today()

findings.title: Plant journal silently stops at 500 entries
findings.steps: A plant with more than 500 entries
findings.actual: The list is fetched with limit=500. Older entries are missing with no indication, while the badge shows the full count.

findings.title: Long unbroken plant names can overflow the Journal feed at 375 px
findings.steps: Create a plant with a long name that has no spaces, add an entry, and view /journal at 375 px
findings.actual: .journal-feed__plant has no overflow-wrap (only the body has overflow-wrap:anywhere), so it can cause horizontal scrolling
